Case name: American Trucking Associations, Inc. v. City of Los Angeles
Court: Supreme Court of the United States
One-sentence holding: Municipal port concession requirements mandating drayage truck placards and off-street parking plans—backed by criminal misdemeanor penalties in tariffs—have the force and effect of law and are preempted by the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act.

Case name: City of Lafayette v. County of Contra Costa
Court: California Court of Appeal, First District
One-sentence holding: Vehicle Code § 21101 does not authorize a city to implement selective street closures (such as an automated gate on Happy Valley Road allowing resident access while barring through commuters); state traffic delegation requires strict construction and prohibits discriminatory street closures (subsequently codified in CVC § 21101.6).

State traffic law fully preempts local regulation; municipalities lack statutory authority under Vehicle Code § 21101 to erect physical traffic barriers (diverters) to selectively close or reroute through-traffic on public residential streets without express legislative authorization.

Case name: City of Poway v. City of San Diego
Court: California Court of Appeal, Fourth District
One-sentence holding: Vehicle Code § 21101(f) does not authorize a city to permanently close a regional roadway (Pomerado Road) to through traffic from an adjoining municipality where the closure impairs regional circulation and contradicts general plan circulation elements.

Case name: Save the Sunset Strip Coalition v. City of West Hollywood
Court: California Court of Appeal, Second District
One-sentence holding: Vehicle Code § 21101 authorizes a municipality to install a cul-de-sac on a local street entirely within its borders to implement the circulation element of its general plan without making a finding that the street is no longer needed for vehicular traffic.

Case name: Citizens for Improved Sorrento Access, Inc. v. City of San Diego
Court: California Court of Appeal, Fourth District
Provision addressed: Cal. Veh. Code § 21101 & Sts. & Hy. Code § 8320
One-sentence holding: A municipality's quasi-legislative determination to close a street to vehicular traffic pursuant to an environmental impact report and general plan amendment is reviewed under the deferential arbitrary-and-capricious standard.

Case name: Neary v. Town of Los Altos Hills
Court: California Court of Appeal, First District
One-sentence holding: A municipal ordinance prohibiting trucks exceeding 12 tons gross weight from all town streets is unconstitutional and unreasonable as applied to a quarry operator lacking alternate routes
Official or database link: exceeding the reasonable exercise of police power under Section 35701.

Case name: National Tank Truck Carriers, Inc. v. City of New York
Court: United States Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
Provision addressed: Hazardous Materials Transportation Act (49 U.S.C. § 5112) & Commerce Clause
One-sentence holding: Municipal fire regulations restricting hazardous material transport across bridges and tunnels to off-peak night hours were not preempted by federal HMTA and did not violate the Commerce Clause where adequate alternate routes exist.

Court: Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division, Bergen County
One-sentence holding: Municipalities lack statutory authority under Title 39 to close municipal side streets to non-residents during rush hours without prior written approval from the Commissioner of Transportation
Official or database link: invalidating Leonia's rush-hour permit closures enacted against Waze traffic.

Court: Supreme Court of the United States
Provision addressed: U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (Dormant Commerce Clause)
One-sentence holding: An Iowa statute prohibiting 65-foot double-trailer trucks on interstate highways violated the Dormant Commerce Clause because the state failed to prove meaningful safety advantages while significantly burdening interstate freight.
